q-29060.name: Question 1
q-29060.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, adding $8$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x-8 & \le 4 \\ -2x-8+8 & \le 4+8 \\ -2x+0 & \le 12 \\ -2x & \le 12\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-2.$ 

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x\,\, & \le \,\,12 \\ \frac{-2x}{-2}\, & \ge \,\,\frac{12}{-2} \\ \frac{\cancel{-2}x}{\cancel{-2}}\, & \ge \,\,-6 \\ x\,\, & \ge \,-6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x\ge -6.$

Question 1
?

Solve the inequality −2x−8≤4.

a
x≥−4
b
x≤−6
c
x≤−4
d
x≥−6
e
x≥2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we apply the addition principle, adding 8 to both sides: −2x−8≤4−2x−8+8≤4+8−2x+0≤12−2x≤12

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by −2.

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

−2x≤12−2x−2≥12−2−2x−2≥−6x≥−6

Therefore, the solution is x≥−6.

q-177678.name: Question 2
q-177678.problem:
The solution to the inequality $-10x-13<17$ is$\,x$
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
q-177678.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, adding $13$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-10x-13 & <17 \\ -10x-13+13 & <17+13 \\ -10x+0 & <30 \\ -10x & <30\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-10.$ 

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-10x\,\, & <\,\,30 \\ \frac{-10x}{-10}\, & >\,\,\frac{30}{-10} \\ \frac{\cancel{-10}x}{\cancel{-10}}\, & >\,\,-3 \\ x\,\, & >\,-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x>-3.$

q-177686.name: Question 3
q-177686.problem: The solution to the inequality $2<9y-7$ is $y${{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
q-177686.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, adding $7$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & <9y-7 \\ 2+7 & <9y-7+7 \\ 9 & <9y+0 \\ 9 & <9y\end{aligned}
$$

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $9:$

$$
\begin{aligned}9 & <9y \\ \frac{9}{9} & <\frac{9y}{9} \\ 1 & <\frac{\cancel{9}y}{\cancel{9}} \\ 1 & <y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let's swap the left and right-hand sides so that the variable is on the left-hand side. Remember, we also need to flip the inequality.

$$
y>1
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y>1.$
